topic.title: FedEx's Founder Took the Last of Its Cash to Las Vegas

title: FedEx Was Down to $5,000. Its Founder Went to Las Vegas
description:
What did FedEx's founder do with the company's last $5,000?
Fred Smith took it to a blackjack table in Las Vegas, told from his own account and FedEx's results.
Sources: Fox Business, FedEx (May 2026).
Based on public records and reporting. Not financial or legal advice.

lines.text: FedEx was down to $5,000. Its founder flew to Vegas.
Fred Smith's Federal Express flew parcels overnight in its own jets. So why was it nearly broke?
In late nineteen seventy-two, Smith had raised $80M, and the fuel bills still ran ahead of it.
When General Dynamics' board refused to put in more, Smith sat down at a blackjack table.
He came back with $27,000. So did a card game save FedEx?
Smith called the win an omen, not the thing that saved it.
With time bought, he raised another $11M, and the jets kept flying.
In the year to May, the company that nearly went under at a blackjack table took in $94.7B.
Luck or nerve: which one saved FedEx? Remember,
